title: feat: worker cutover to the replica feed and governor relay (W-OBS W4)
body:
Part of #2468

W-OBS W4 (spec `w-obs-spec.md` section 9, row W4): the worker cutover and the governor relay, in one PR as D9/Q-G require.

**Cutover.** `ReplicaCutover` and its factory are deleted; every worker now builds the replica client. The section 6.2 readers (app HTTP admission gate, drain gate, node-reported state, governor eligibility) resolve to `ReplicaReadiness.ready()`; `authorizePassiveClient` is deleted from `RabiaEngine` and `RabiaNode` (I-W6). TW-O3, TW-O9 and TW-O12 are flipped, `EmberIncarnationWiringTest` is rewritten, `ReplicaCutoverGateTest` is flipped (dark assertions removed with the type; the governor-first test is `ReplicaFeedClientRelayTest.aMemberWithAnAnnouncedServingGovernor_neverSubscribesToACore`). The two forge `Hierarchical*` heavy tests now black out the replica feed messages instead of the metadata ones. The metadata projection channel stays (it no longer polls or drives anything); W5 deletes it.

**Relay.** `ReplicaServeGate` (I-W5), `UpstreamSelector` governor arm (I-W8, the silence switch goes through the same call), the hand-off on the `isGovernor()` edge (read from the client's tick, so `GovernorAnnouncer`/`GovernorAuthority`/`GovernorElection`/`HierarchyPeerPolicy` link rules and `SpokesmanPingLoop` are untouched), `BUSY` handling, a governor serves only members of its own community. A governor that failed a session is left alone for 10 s `[guess]`.

**Decisions I took, marked as guesses (change in review)**
1. Spec 2.8 readiness (reviewer's patch adopted): a resume to another source carries the counted heartbeats for one silence interval (3 s) only, or until the new source counts its own, so a healthy re-parent shows no blip and a dead source stops readiness within the bound; through the relay both cores gone ends the governor at about 8 s and its member at about 13 s (was 60 s before the review).
2. A source whose store was reset (stopping, restarting empty) answers `NOT_SERVING`, not `INCARNATION_MISMATCH` (spec section 5 row 17). Found in Ember: the mismatch made every member of a killed governor discard its position and re-snapshot (about 3 s readiness gap and a snapshot burst).
3. A node dismisses its subscribers with `NOT_SERVING` once it stops serving.
4. A member follows the announced governor only while it has a link to it (`connectedPeers()`): a subscribe over a link that is not up is lost without a refusal and costs the 3 s silence. Found by the 50-worker read-out (below); link rules unchanged.

**Governor ring window (W1 ring code, not changed):** after a snapshot install a node's ring is empty (`clearTo` clears the anchor), so a governor refuses an anchored member `EVICTED` until the cluster commits an effect batch past the member's newest pair; in a quiet cluster that can be long. Members' fallback (pinned): a governor's refusal of any reason, or a heartbeat behind the member, keeps the member's position and sends it back to a core, which resumes it from the anchor (no snapshot); the governor is asked again every 10 s. The window therefore costs one refused subscribe per member per 10 s, never a snapshot. A snapshot the governor itself serves in that window is unanchored (an ordinary join, tag and SHA-256 checked).

**Evidence** (cloudbb-3; files in oss `internal/rc5-planning/wave3/wobs-w4-*`)
- New behavioural tests: `ReplicaFeedClientRelayTest` (12: governor-first, rebalance, NT-O21 governor dies, NT-O23 core dies, NT-O29 deposed governor, NT-O30 slow member, NT-O31 a/b, NT-O34 join storm, retry interval, hand-off, self), `ReplicaServeGateTest`, `ReplicaReadinessTest.servable*`, `ReplicaFeedServerTest` (dismiss, reset), `ReplicaFeedAssemblyTest`, and `EmberReplicaRelayTest` (5 cores + 27 workers in 2 communities: members follow governors, NT-O44 over a governor with a control, a governor killed under 100 ms write load: no surviving member ever seen not ready, re-parent, converge; a core killed mid-snapshot). The Ember test is green 6 of 6 runs at its final shape on cloudbb-3, and green in the Ember CI shards.
- Per-changed-line mutation (cluster, node, Ember): all RED except equivalent mutants stated in the file. Review round: the three serve-gate wires are now pinned by `ReplicaClientAssemblyTest.serveGate_needsEachOfItsThreeTerms_wiredFromTheirOwnObjects` (B1-B3 RED), hand-off on a core session and rebalance during a join have tests (C2, C4 RED), the chain test `whenBothCoresAreGone_*` is red without the carry limit (K1-K2), `fellBackFromGovernor`/`behindOrAhead` are pinned (F1, F2 RED; F3 `avoided.add` is equivalent, the retry delay already excludes the governor).
- 50-worker M-OBS read-out, interleaved A/B on one host (base = rc5 with the LIVE seam): after the fix head and base are indistinguishable (all-ready 4.5-4.7 s both at today's host load; 0 silence switches). The first head run regressed (all-ready 5.7-7.3 s, 6-28 silence switches): that is finding 4.
- jbct `mvn jbct:check -Djbct.skip=false`: "Running JBCT check on 87 / 65 / 241 / 6 Java file(s)" (consensus / cluster / node / ember), rc=0; `jbct:format` applied once.
- Suites at the final code head (consensus, cluster, node and their 80 upstream modules, 83-module reactor, cloudbb-3, 2753 s): 21245 `<testcase>` elements in 3720 XML newer than the run marker, 0 failures, 0 errors, 52 skipped; consensus 1397, cluster 428, node 4350. The CI build-and-test failure on cae1bb258c was an unrelated stash pop that swept an 18-line deletion in `ClusterBootstrapConfigParser` into the shard-weights commit; reverted in a61c58a20e (net aether-config diff against the base is empty).

**Not done / limits.** RED at base for the new tests is a compile failure (new types); the behavioural gate is the mutation of the governor arm, which turns `ReplicaFeedClientRelayTest` and `EmberReplicaRelayTest` red. Heap per worker and rolling deploy / delivery read-outs not repeated. The rolling-upgrade break of W2 still applies.

title: fix: KV-derived cluster events are gated on the committed ownership record (#1671)
body:
Closes #1671

PR-7a of the streams overhaul (spec 14.5, invariant I-35). Acceptance from #1671: two nodes straddling a handover produce exactly one copy of a KV-derived fact in a deterministic test; the at-least-once pin stays green; the drop case (neither side passes) is covered by a test that fails today.

**The gate.** `ClusterEventAggregator.emitCommitted` gates a fact derived from a committed KV notification on state every node holds identically at that notification:
1. the owner named by the committed `StreamPartitionOwnershipKey` of `system:cluster-events:1.0.0` partition 0, as of that notification (`onStreamPartitionOwnershipPut` records it; its removal, which a snapshot install synthesises, clears it: `onStreamPartitionOwnershipRemove`);
2. with no record, the leader named by the committed `LeaderKey` as of that notification (`onLeaderCommitted`);
3. a node that has seen neither notification yet reads the same two records from the store;
4. with none of these (an unbound aggregator, nothing committed), the node-local `ownerCheck`, as `emit` does.

KV notifications are dispatched in commit order, so a recorded value read inside a later handler is the value at that index; a read of the live store could be ahead of it. The no-record rule changed in the second round: the first version used the lowest member of the installed voter configuration, which a lagging node adopts ahead of its KV apply (`adoptSyncedConfiguration`), so two nodes could hold different rosters at one index (v-2500 T1: a duplicate and a drop; test `ClusterEvents_noRecord_nodesHoldingDifferentRosters_raiseExactlyOneCopy`, red at `97cf170163`). The spec text said "lowest NodeId of the committed core membership"; no KV key carries a committed roster, so the committed leader is the deterministic stand-in (a guess, marked as such in I-35).

**Scope.** The three KV handlers use it: `onNodeArtifactPut` (`DeploymentStarted/Completed/Failed`), `onCommunityPut`, `onGovernorAnnouncementPut`. Everything else keeps `emit` and the node-local gate: ISR transitions, `ConnectionEstablished/Failed`, `AccessDenied`, scaling (not KV-derived; their residual duplicate or drop is unchanged and pinned by a test). Config and blueprint events are single-origin API facts raised on the node that served the request, not KV-derived; the ownership gate drops them on every non-owner request node, a different and larger hole, ticketed as #2503.

**Limit, stated.** A record that names a dead owner suppresses the facts on every surviving node until the next ownership record (or, with no record, the next leader record): the gate is strictly the record, with no liveness fallback and no queue, logged at DEBUG as "not owner". `[unverified: window length]`. The node-local gate it replaces depended on the same new owner, since the stream publish needs it too.

**Tests.** `ClusterEventAggregatorCommittedGateTest` (first commit red at rc5: 4 of 5): exactly one copy with both local views claiming the partition, the mirrored schedule, a node the record does not name raises none, the decision follows the notification order, the leader rule, removal of the record, the empty case, every KV handler, replay suppression, the non-KV fact still gated node-locally. `ClusterEventsCommittedGateBootTest` (v-2500 T2) boots a real node and pins the production wiring: the leader route, the ownership removal route, and the store lookups bound in `ClusterEventsAssembly` (with the call removed it goes red). The at-least-once pin `emit_ownerHandover_bothOwnersRaiseOneFact_eachRaiseIsDeliveredAtLeastOnce` goes through `emit` and is untouched.

**The three points that were `[unverified]` in the spec:** (1) one commit-ordered notification stream: confirmed by v-2500 (a FIFO queue drained under the store lock, a synchronous router, all four handlers on one `kvRouterBuilder`); (2) the voter configuration is updated in step with KV notifications: false, fixed here by not using it; (3) removal of the ownership record: handled by `onStreamPartitionOwnershipRemove`.

title: feat: streams PR-0b part 2 — expired segment blocks leave every tier, the DHT included, under a durable shared-delete authority (part of #2258)
body:
Part of #2258 (does not close it: the DHT bound and its accounting are 0b-3, which closes #2258). Streams overhaul spec draft 6, §3.2 items 5 and 6, and the two delete codes of item 8. This is part 2 of PR-0b (CTO split, 2026-10-29), as ruled by `know:` `d19f755873`: no footprint sweep, `adopt` unchanged, and only an explicit destroy (`forget`) releases `IF_IDENTIFIED`.

**Flag days (pre-GA, spec 1.4):**
- **Segment blocks:** every new block starts with an identity header, `MAGIC2`. A new node reads every older form (no magic, `MAGIC`, `MAGIC2`). An old node misreads a `MAGIC2` block as events, so a mixed cluster must not share segments. Upgrade by coordinated replacement.
- **Metadata snapshots (downgrade only):** a lifecycle line may carry two new flags, `SHARED_DELETE_AUTHORISED` and `SHARED_DELETE_IF_IDENTIFIED`, in the same optional eighth field as `CACHE_ONLY`. A build without them refuses that snapshot and falls back to an older retained one. A record without a flag is written byte-for-byte as before.
- **No wire change.**

## What changes
- **Storage** (`integrations/storage`):
  - `BlockLifecycle.sharedDelete` (`NONE` / `AUTHORISED` / `IF_IDENTIFIED`) is set only when a scoped `deleteRef(name, authority)` orphans the block, and cleared by any re-credit.
  - `StorageInstance.deleteEverywhere` uses the GC's compare-and-remove claim, deletes the shared tier FIRST and the private tiers after, and puts the record back on any failure. An `IF_IDENTIFIED` orphan is read and goes the shared way only if the instance's identification predicate accepts its bytes.
  - `StorageGarbageCollector.collectSharedDeletes(snapshots, limits)` forces a snapshot (only when there are candidates). It deletes only orphans whose authority is in THAT snapshot and that are past a 2-minute grace, 8 at a time, at most 10,000 blocks or 60 s a run.
  - The periodic tick leaves flagged orphans alone, so it never deletes them privately and leaks the DHT copy (MT-60).
  - The pressure path deletes everywhere only a durably flagged orphan. A not-yet-durable one is left (R32D-01).
  - Restore resets the authority of any record that a restored ref names (R32D-13).
  - `TierScope.PRIVATE` on `putRef`/`replaceRef`. It falls back to every tier, counted, when there is no private durable tier.
- **Streams:**
  - `SegmentProvenance.withIdentity` writes `[MAGIC2][durable name (carries the incarnation)][partition][start][end][slice count or -1][slice][events]`; `split` reads all three forms; `isIdentified` is the instance predicate, wired in `StorageFactory`.
  - `SegmentRef.identity` takes one of three values. `IDENTIFIED` is set at seal. `UNKNOWN` means rebuilt; the age read then learns `IDENTIFIED` or `LEGACY`.
  - Retention drops the segment from the index first, then releases its ref:
    - `AUTHORISED` when identified;
    - `IF_IDENTIFIED` when unknown;
    - no authority when legacy.
    A failed release puts the segment back and stops the partition's pass, and the in-memory floor advances only past segments actually released.
  - Floors and cursor commits write `PRIVATE`.
  - A rebuild or an adopt no longer serves a ref at or below its partition's durable reclaim floor. The ref is drained and released `IF_IDENTIFIED` (NT-122).
  - `StreamFootprint.forget` releases `IF_IDENTIFIED`; `adopt` releases no other life.
  - `SharedSegmentCollection`: the streams instance's own run, every 60 s, separate from the 5-minute maintenance tick. It is owned, started and closed by the retention enforcer, so a node runs it from start to stop. It raises `stream-segment-delete-failing` after 3 consecutive failing runs, and closes it with `stream-segment-delete-recovered`.

Rc5 is no worse after this PR. Nothing is deleted from any tier that today's code would keep, except:
- the blocks of segments retention has already released;
- a destroyed stream's blocks;
- ref-less blocks below a durable floor.

## RED (first commit `e278c30d63`; the API surface is present and keeps today's behaviour: interface defaults, no override, no pruning, no warnings, base sink)
Run at the RED commit on bigboy:
- `SharedDeleteCollectionTest`: 10 of 14 tests.
- `SegmentSharedDeleteTest`: 7 of 11 tests.
- `SegmentProvenanceTest` identity cases (2).
- `StreamSegmentDhtReclaimTest`: both tests (NT-120 at node level).
- Header-shaped expectations (seven tests):
  - `StorageSegmentSinkTest`;
  - `SegmentCompressionEncryptionTest` (3 tests);
  - `RetentionAgeAfterRestartTest` (2 tests);
  - `DiskPressureRestartTest`.

Green at RED by design: the controls, the hazard tests, and the codes, census and docs (data).

## Verification at the head (bigboy)
- **Suites (on rc5 `f9a3893de9` plus this branch):** `integrations/storage` 962/0, `aether-stream` 2141/0, node targeted 303/0 (`StreamSegmentDhtReclaimTest`, `StorageMaintenanceWiringTest`, `RetentionScheduleBootTest`, `ClusterEventAggregatorTest`, `OperatorWarningCodeDocsTest`, `StorageFactory*Test`, wire tests).
- **Hazard tests:**
  - `aSegmentInsideItsRetention_neverLeavesAnyTier`;
  - `afterAColdRestartWithAnEmptyCommittedSet_nothingIsDeleted` (CTO's case: rebuild, a source that answers nothing, three passes and runs, nothing deleted);
  - `aLegacySegment_neverLeavesTheSharedTier`;
  - `aRefBelowTheDurableFloor…` (the legacy shared copy stays);
  - `aReleaseThatLeavesAnotherReference_recordsNoAuthority`;
  - `anAuthorityNotYetInTheDurableSnapshot_isNotActedOn`.
- **Mutation probes, 17 of 17 RED on their expected tests** (controls green; the new NT-120 arm's control was run separately, 2/0; run at `fc01bd75c9`, before the rebase onto rc5, which changed no patch: `git range-diff` shows only context next to the new warning codes):
  - MT-46 (ref drop only), MT-47 (no durable check), MT-48 (no header), MT-50 (installs below floor), MT-55 (cursor `ALL`), MT-60 (tick takes flagged), MT-61 (re-credit keeps the flag), MT-62 (forget without authority), MT-63 (pressure path ignores the flag), MT-64 (restore keeps the flag), MT-65 (`IF_IDENTIFIED` read as `AUTHORISED`);
  - plus six more: private tiers deleted first, no time bound, a warning on every failing run, the predicate not wired, a private write landing on every tier, a failed release not put back.
  - after the rebase, the private-put refactor (JBCT-TOT-02) was probed again: a private claim that always falls back went RED on `aPrivateWrite_landsOnPrivateTiersOnly_andItsRecordSaysSo`.

## Reconciliation with spec draft 6 §3.2 (11.1)
| Spec | This PR | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Item 6: footprint sweep, `adopt` releases other lives; NT-137, MT-66 | none; `adopt` releases no other life; NT-137 and MT-66 dropped | `know:` `d19f755873` (contradicts `6d0c58fd67`; `onStateRestored` also fires on an empty committed set after a cold restart without `[backup]`). L-15 stands until PR-8j/#2458 |
| (not in spec) | `adopt` releases the ADOPTED life's own refs at or below its own durable floor | Lives with a minted incarnation are installed at `adopt`, not at rebuild, so NT-122's below-floor case surfaces there. This is retention finishing its own durable reclaim. No other life is touched. Flagged for the verifier |
| Item 6: the lifecycle authority as "an eighth, trailing value an older reader ignores" | new `LineFlag` values in the existing optional 8th field | at rc5 field 8 is parsed as a `LineFlag` and an unknown flag fails the snapshot (`DefaultSnapshotManager`, by design); the spec's premise was wrong. Downgrade-only consequence stated above |
| Item 6: `sharedDelete` recorded "when the count reaches 0" | recorded only on the transition from referenced to orphaned | a redundant release of an already-orphaned block keeps the authority it was orphaned with |
| Item 5: header field `incarnation:8` if the durable name lacks it | not needed | the durable name carries the incarnation (`SegmentIndex.durableName`, `<stream>@<incarnation>`) |
| Item 5: "both magics are negative, no event block is mistaken" | `split` compares the magic exactly | the code tests equality, not sign; both remain negative longs |
| Item 6: "a read of its range now answers `CursorExpired`" | holds while a newer sealed segment exists; with nothing sealed above, today's empty answer | `TieredStreamReader.read` (unchanged) |
| Item 6: an encrypted block | sealed by this build: marked and deleted; released after a restart before the mark is learned: kept (stored bytes are ciphertext) | the predicate reads stored bytes; each encrypted seal gets its own block id from its fresh IV anyway |
| Item 6: "the GC is given the instance's `SnapshotManager`" | passed per run (`collectSharedDeletes(snapshots, limits)`) | the collector stays independent of the manager's lifecycle |
| Item 6: the separate run every minute | `SharedSegmentCollection`, owned by the enforcer | so the boot test of 0b-1 (`RetentionScheduleBootTest`) covers its lifecycle; [unverified: not separately asserted at boot] |
| Item 5: a fallback counted | `StorageInstance.privateScopeFallbacks()` | no gauge yet |
| NT-121 (Ember, two arms) | component level: `DHTDurableDeleteTest#removeMissedByOneReplica_isNotResurrectedByAntiEntropy`, `#expiredTombstone_isCollectedOnlyAfterEveryCoReplicaAgrees`, `#nodeRemovedWhileRunning_rejoinsEmpty_afterTheTombstoneWasCollected`; `DhtStorageTierTest` (delete reaches the client) | gating item 2 allowed component level; the DHT code is unchanged by this PR |
| NT-127: survives a restart 10 s after a commit | not separately tested | the commit's ref durability is unchanged (snapshot-backed as before); only the tier scope changed |
| NT-130: the adopt arm | inverted: adopt keeps the other life | the ruling |
| NT-139: the maintenance tick still demotes | the run's time bound is tested (`aSlowSharedTier…`); the separation from the tick is by construction | [unverified: not run with a hung DHT] |
| MT-56 (DHT remove local-only) | not probed here | DHT code unchanged; pinned by `DHTDurableDeleteTest` |
| MT-57 (inline delete before the index drop) | not expressible against this design | ordering pinned instead: private-first (x1) and the put-back on a failed release (x6) |
| Item 8 | `DELETE_FAILING`/`RECOVERED` only | `NEAR_FULL`, `FULL` and `DISK_PRESSURE` belong to 0b-3 |

## Not in this PR
- Item 7: the DHT bound, its byte accounting and `TierFull`. That is 0b-3, which closes #2258.
- PR-3c: checkpoint-block reclaim. Entity checkpoint blocks still leak into `stream-segments/`.
- No release ships PR-0b without PR-1a (Q14).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Expired or explicitly destroyed stream segments are reclaimed from private and shared storage after the release is durable and the grace period has passed.
  * New segments carry identity information to help protect shared blocks and legacy segments from unintended deletion.
  * Stream floors and consumer cursors use private storage when available.
  * Reclamation resumes after restart for segments below durable reclaim floors.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Reclamation stops safely when a segment release fails, preserving progress for a later attempt.
* **Operations**
  * Repeated deletion failures raise a warning; a successful run emits a recovery event.
